open_points.subject: Disclosure class of an empty mapped operation output
open_points.text: A07 rule 3 says a binding output takes the class the binding declares “for the empty lists of a mapped operation over an empty list alike”; A13 rule 6 says “an empty list takes the highest class among the node's inputs”.
open_points.question: When a mapped operation receives an empty list, is each empty output list classified from the binding output declaration or from the node's inputs?
options: Use the binding output port's declared class
Use the highest class among the mapped node's inputs
open_points.default_guess: Use the binding output port's declared class because A07 states the operation-specific rule explicitly.

open_points.subject: Class record for an empty many-file output
open_points.text: A13 says “An empty list is named, with its class, by the one NodeExecution”, but M23 represents file outputs only as “SpooledFiles by their facts”; an empty file list has no SpooledFile carrying a class.
open_points.question: Where is the disclosure class of an empty `many` file output recorded so it can be recovered after restart and used by A07?
options: Add a class-bearing per-port list reference to NodeExecution
Derive the class from the node and binding or input records
Forbid empty `many` file outputs
open_points.default_guess: Store a class-bearing per-port reference in the NodeExecution.

open_points.subject: Redacted failure-detail length
open_points.text: A07 rule 5 says a protected `failure_detail` is returned to an agent “only as its length and that class” without defining the unit of length.
open_points.question: Is the reported failure-detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit, and is it measured before or after A20 truncation?
options: UTF-8 bytes after truncation
Unicode code points after truncation
Original UTF-8 bytes before truncation
open_points.default_guess: Report UTF-8 bytes after truncation, matching the release ceilings.

open_points.subject: Trial-execution failure details
open_points.text: A03 says the kernel keeps exception type and message as `failure_detail`, and A07 defines disclosure of an execution's `failure_detail`, but M07 TrialExecution has no `failure_detail` field, only `detail_code`.
open_points.question: Do trial executions retain a bounded failure detail; if so, in which model field is it stored and subjected to A07 disclosure?
options: Add `failure_detail` to TrialExecution
Keep failure details only for run NodeExecutions
Encode all trial failure information solely in `detail_code`
open_points.default_guess: Add the same bounded `failure_detail` field to TrialExecution and apply A07 to it.

open_points.subject: Credential non-occurrence versus equal ordinary data
open_points.text: A17 says the kernel never puts a resolved credential value into any store, preview, trace or response, while A10 requires previews to contain ordinary input values and required-header values; either may coincidentally equal the credential bytes.
open_points.question: Is the secrecy guarantee provenance-based, excluding only the value read as a credential, or must the kernel detect and withhold every byte-for-byte occurrence of that value regardless of its source?
options: Provenance-based: omit only the credential header value
Byte-based: scan and withhold matching inputs, headers and outputs
Reject a request whenever non-credential data equals the credential
open_points.default_guess: Treat the guarantee as byte-based because A17's invariant and canary test are stated in terms of verbatim occurrence.

open_points.subject: Encoded service echoes of credentials
open_points.text: State 0 says secrets “never enter a function, a flow, a trace or an answer”; A17 rule 2 says an echo “in another encoding is not recognised, and is protected only by its class,” allowing it to be stored and returned when its declared class permits.
open_points.question: May a service response containing an encoded form of a credential enter stored values, traces or answers, or must the State 0 no-secret guarantee also cover encoded forms?
options: Only verbatim credential bytes are prohibited
Recognisable common encodings are also prohibited
No service response derived from a credential may be retained
open_points.default_guess: Apply the later operational rule and prohibit only verbatim credential bytes, while treating this as a narrowing that the texts must state explicitly.

open_points.subject: Credential control-character refusal
open_points.text: A17 rule 2 refuses a credential that “holds ... a control character” without defining that set.
open_points.question: Exactly which Unicode characters or encoded bytes count as control characters after UTF-8 decoding and removal of one trailing newline?
options: HTTP CTLs: U+0000–U+001F and U+007F
Every Unicode General Category Cc character
Only CR, LF and NUL
open_points.default_guess: Use the HTTP CTL set U+0000–U+001F and U+007F because the value is sent as an HTTP header.

open_points.subject: Retry eligibility after a waiting attempt
open_points.text: A13 rule 2 says a mapped element runs only when it “has no concluded record” and that “a concluded element is never executed again”; A09 and A14 require an element with a `service_unreachable` NodeExecution to be sent again on resume, and A11 requires a resend after an `outcome_unknown` attempt resolved `not_applied`.
open_points.question: What precisely makes an element eligible for another attempt despite an existing immutable NodeExecution, and what does “concluded record” mean here?
options: Only terminal element conclusions prevent another attempt; waiting outcomes may retry
Any NodeExecution prevents retry, contradicting resume and resend
Track an explicit current-attempt lifecycle separate from historical NodeExecutions
open_points.default_guess: Treat only terminal element conclusions as preventing another attempt; waiting outcomes retain historical records but remain retryable.

open_points.subject: Ordering derived skip and upstream-failure records against executable nodes
open_points.text: A13 fixes the next ready executable node and A15 orders records “that become non-executable together”, but neither says whether newly derivable `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed` records are written before or after an independent ready node executes, nor how successive propagation waves interleave.
open_points.question: When execution makes some nodes non-executable while other nodes are ready, in what deterministic order are derived records and executable nodes processed?
options: Exhaust all newly derivable records in node/map order before executing another ready node
Execute the smallest ready node first, then derive non-executable records
Choose the smallest node across both executable and derivable conclusions
open_points.default_guess: Choose the smallest node across executable work and derivable conclusions, using the stated map-index ordering for elements.
